overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the March 2012 executive sessions fit litigation Purpose 3 and no deliberation occurred outside a posted meeting, though the chair omitted a required declaration.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that March 12 and March 26, 2012 executive sessions covered the Town's purchase of a mobile home park, outside the stated litigation-strategy purpose.
allegations.key_passage: The Board's executive session discussions were appropriate under Purpose 3 because they related to a pending lawsuit filed against the Town.

allegations.summary: Alternatively alleged that the Board deliberated on the same lawsuit outside a properly posted meeting, including through agenda-setting contact among officials.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, we did not find any evidence that the Board engaged in deliberation outside of a properly posted meeting regarding the lawsuit.

allegations.summary: AG noted, without finding a violation, that the chair omitted the required Purpose 3 declaration that an open meeting would harm the Board's litigating position.
allegations.key_passage: The Board generally followed the requisite procedures for entering executive session; however, we note that the Chair failed to make the statement required under Purpose 3 that an open meeting would have a detrimental effect on the litigating position of the public body.
